notes: Specific-performance/adverse-possession dispute over vacant unenclosed lots and a defective mortgage foreclosure; no letting or lodging of a dwelling at issue. Selector matched generic 'right' language, not a lease/letting fact pattern.
Dispute over whether a deed absolute plus side agreement constituted a mortgage; concerns partnership real estate held as security, not any lodging or dwelling-letting arrangement.
Trade-name/unfair-competition dispute between stamp and coin dealers; no occupancy of a dwelling or rooms is involved. Selector matched generic language about honest intent, unrelated to lodging.

Injunction case enforcing a mid-19th-century building-setback covenant among adjoining lot owners; the 'incident of ownership' language concerns a husband's marital-era power to bind his wife's land by covenant, not letting of rooms for occupancy.
Appeal in the same Bradley v. Walker setback-covenant litigation (see case_id 1695846); addresses purchaser notice of a recorded covenant and an extra costs allowance, not dwelling letting.
Fire insurance policy assignment/consent-to-transfer dispute following sale of the insured dwelling; the transfer is a conveyance of ownership, not a letting or lodging arrangement.

Hotel lessees' furniture was pledged as security to the landlord's assignee and later seized under a bank's chattel mortgage; dispute is purely about lien/mortgage priority on hotel chattels. No holding addresses the character or regulation of guest lodging.

Holds a sleeping-car (Pullman) company to ordinary-carrier, not innkeeper, liability for a passenger's lost overcoat. Discusses innkeeper-liability doctrine only to distinguish it; a railroad sleeping berth is transportation, not letting of a dwelling/room, so it falls outside the corpus's scope despite touching 'innkeeping' vocabulary.

court: New York Supreme Court, General Term
notes: Summary landlord-tenant proceeding over a monthly fee paid for using a derrick/scales/office on a public pier berth; court holds no landlord-tenant relation arose. Concerns wharf equipment, not dwelling/room occupancy.

court: New York Supreme Court, General Term
notes: Construction of a guaranty covenant tied to a one-sixteenth ownership share in a schooner's earnings; 'incident of ownership' refers to ship earnings, unrelated to letting of dwellings or rooms.

court: New York Supreme Court, General Term

court: New York Supreme Court, General Term

court: New York Supreme Court, General Term

court: New York Supreme Court, General Term
notes: In re Jacobs: strikes down an 1884 act banning cigar manufacture in tenement-house rooms used as a home, as an invalid deprivation of the right to labor in one's own residence. Addresses use of a dwelling for one's own trade, not compensated letting of rooms to lodgers/boarders — a different (though doctrinally adjacent) property-rights question, so treated as irrelevant to this corpus's occupancy-for-pay focus.
Riparian water-rights/diversion dispute between adjoining mill-lot owners; 'incident of ownership' refers to the right to a stream's natural flow, not to letting of dwellings or rooms.

Seduction action by a mother who kept a boarding house on her separate account, turning on a married woman's statutory standing to sue for loss of her daughter/servant's services. Division-fence dispute under the fence-viewer statute, including whether land was left to 'lie open to a public common'; concerns farm boundary fencing, not dwelling letting.

Replevin case on a married woman's right under the 1848-49/1860 acts to purchase goods and carry on a general flour/feed trade through her husband as agent; a general married-women's-property-and-commerce case with no dwelling or lodging occupancy at issue.
